references.text: The same command to write God's words on the doorposts and gates is found in the Shema passage, which forms the basis of the Jewish mezuzah tradition.
Israel was commanded to smear blood on the doorposts during the Passover in Egypt, illustrating the symbolic significance of doorposts within the covenant relationship.
The command to have God's words as a sign on the hand and between the eyes is connected with writing them on the doorposts.
Joshua wrote the words of the law on stones, a parallel practice to writing God's words in visible places as a reminder.
Isaiah mentions that the people set up their memorial markers behind the door and at the doorpost, contrasting with the proper use of doorposts for God's words.
